label: Reference and coverage audit
title: Version 3: proved statements, replacements, and unfinished results

source.title: Proximal Interacting Particle Langevin Algorithms, arXiv:2406.14292v3

checks.claim: Version 3 supersedes the originally linked version 1.
checks.note: PIPGLA in v3 targets the original nonsmooth model. The squared-gradient particle scaling was corrected between versions. No v1-only issue is attributed to v3.

checks.claim: The proximity map is the minimizer of the original quadratic objective.
checks.note: Existence, uniqueness, residual optimality and firm nonexpansiveness are derived for finite-valued convex lower-bounded functions on finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.

checks.claim: The actual Moreau envelope is continuously differentiable with residual gradient and smoothness 1/λ.
checks.note: The derivative follows from proved lower-support and quadratic upper bounds; it is not assumed through an abstract envelope interface.

checks.claim: For K-Lipschitz g₂, the value gap is between 0 and λK²/2.
checks.note: The bound is uniform and finite, obtained by completing a square. It requires no Hessian.

checks.claim: MYIPLA is exactly the scaled IPLA recursion for g₁+g₂^λ.
checks.note: Coordinate identities, iterated maps and Gaussian-law identities identify the actual algorithm. Noise and initialization independence remain explicit.

checks.claim: PIPGLA takes a noisy smooth step followed by averaged joint proximal maps.
checks.note: Exact coordinate maps, measurable L² recursions, finite moments, probability laws and canonical independent-Gaussian law transfer are proved.

checks.claim: The split potential g₁+g₂^λ remains m-strongly convex with gradient constant L₁+1/λ.
checks.note: Convexity and gradient smoothness of the actual envelope are derived, then added to the g₁ assumptions.

checks.claim: MYIPLA approaches the original marginal maximizer with concentration, transient, discretization and smoothing terms.
checks.note: The actual-law theorem uses √(λK²/m), sharp √(dθ/(Nm)), explicit Lλ and a discrete contraction. It does not reproduce the paper’s O(λ)+O(λ²) smoothing expression or claim a smoothing-independent discretization constant.

checks.claim: The paper claims a linear asymptotic distance between original and smoothed marginal maximizers.
checks.note: The formal bound is √(λK²/m), derived from a uniform value gap and strong-convexity growth. The stronger conclusion is not claimed false merely because its displayed proof has gaps.

checks.claim: The interacting smoothed SDE has a unique strong solution.
checks.note: The shared Langevin development constructs the stationary reference needed by the actual MYIPLA theorem. That does not reproduce this precise strong-solution existence-and-uniqueness statement as a separate result.

checks.claim: The smoothed Gibbs measure is invariant for the continuous interacting system.
checks.note: The actual MYIPLA proof invokes the existing IPLA/ULA construction of a continuous stationary Gibbs reference after deriving the smoothed potential assumptions. Euler-step stationarity is not claimed.

checks.claim: The powered smoothed marginal concentrates near the original marginal maximizer.
checks.note: Sharp concentration about the smoothed maximizer is proved; the transfer to the original center uses the finite square-root smoothing estimate.

checks.claim: PIPULA is MYIPLA with g₁=0 and λ=γ.
checks.note: Both the exact update identity and full recursion identity are established.

checks.claim: PIPULA satisfies the paper’s original-center finite-time convergence estimate.
checks.note: The algorithm reduction, full-envelope strong convexity and corrected B1 implication are available, but the stated scale-uniform discretization/original-center theorem is not.

checks.claim: The full envelope of an m-strongly convex potential has modulus m/(1+mλ).
checks.note: The exact reduced modulus is proved directly from proximal minimizers and a completed weighted square; it is distinct from preservation of m by split smoothing.

checks.paper_location: Assumption B1 and following sentence, p. 18
checks.claim: A proximal inner-product deficit μ implies envelope-gradient strong monotonicity μ/γ.
checks.note: The residual gradient is divided by γ. The exact implication with μ/γ is formalized; the paper’s sentence writes μ without that division.

checks.claim: The smooth forward step has the displayed transport-energy decrease.
checks.status: not reproduced as this law theorem
checks.note: The existing strong-convexity ULA/IPLA proof has its own contraction argument. The precise law-level smooth-energy statement is not exported here.

checks.claim: A proximal step decreases squared distance and nonsmooth energy up to λ² times a bounded input subgradient norm.
checks.note: Actual proximal optimality and genuine support subgradients imply the energy estimate; no energy/convergence bound is assumed.

checks.claim: The deterministic proximal energy inequality lifts to the displayed W₂ law inequality.
checks.status: actual L² energy proved; source transport route not reproduced
checks.note: The genuine pointwise averaged-particle energy inequality is integrated with proved finite moments. The subsequent stochastic recurrence is derived by canonical synchronous coupling rather than assuming the paper’s lifted proximal identity.

checks.claim: Gaussian convolution obeys the heat-flow entropy evolution variational inequality.
checks.note: The exact published heat-flow transport/entropy result is not reproduced. The actual PIPGLA replacement instead derives its law recurrence from a constructed synchronous coupling; it does not assume this entropy statement.

checks.claim: The free-energy difference is KL with respect to the original nonsmooth Gibbs target.
checks.note: The required density, entropy and energy integrability identities for the splitting analysis remain to be established. Existing conditional LSI data are not substituted for them.

checks.claim: The combined splitting step satisfies the paper’s KL–W₂ inequality.
checks.note: Deterministic proximal components do not establish this law-level theorem without the heat-entropy and free-energy bridges.

checks.claim: Iterating the affine error recurrence gives a finite sum and geometric error floor.
checks.note: The recurrence is an explicit hypothesis. The statement is not attached to actual PIPGLA laws. Strict q<1 is required for a finite floor.

checks.claim: Noise scaled by 1/√N gives forcing λ(2γL₁D/N+λC).
checks.note: Version 3 correctly uses N²C after scaling the gradient and λNC in its unsimplified numerator. This corrects v1, not v3. A stochastic law theorem is not inferred from the scalar formula alone.

checks.paper_location: Roadmap item 3, p. 19; Corollary A.13, p. 24
checks.claim: The averaged pairwise proximal step has the required energy inequality for the original lifted potential.
checks.note: Averaged pairwise proximity generally differs from proximity of the lifted sum. Jensen on the common parameter plus the single-pair energy estimate proves exactly the needed deterministic bridge.

checks.claim: The actual PIPGLA particle law satisfies the final squared-transport estimate.
checks.note: The genuine original-center RMS bound is proved through an alternative coupling argument, with conservative constants. The exact printed corollary is not reproduced.

checks.claim: A continuous strongly convex Gibbs law has second moment about its mode at most dimension divided by modulus.
checks.note: The proof uses sharp radial growth and dilation, avoiding an assumed noncompact integration-by-parts identity. The actual smooth marginal specialization gives dθ/(Nm).

checks.claim: PIPGLA has the stated original-model parameter RMS convergence bound.
checks.note: Actual-law convergence follows from a constructed stationary Brownian coupling and an infimum over finite-cost couplings. The reference ΠNγ is smoothed, then a finite center shift reaches the original maximizer. An explicit γ-independent coefficient and K|λ−γ|/(mγ) sensitivity term replace the printed numerical formula; no recurrence or stationarity is assumed.

checks.claim: MYPGD satisfies the displayed parameter-error bound.
checks.note: The actual latent-noise MYPGD law is compared with the actual MYIPLA law by a derived Gaussian Markov coupling. Squared W₂ comparison cost≤2dθ/(Nm) gives an original-center theorem. This is a conservative replacement with Gibbs initial-law transient, not the source’s mean-field metric/constants or Taylor bias; no propagation-of-chaos rate is assumed.

checks.claim: The averaged smoothed drift is Lipschitz with coefficient 1/λ.
checks.note: The actual Bochner expectation is integrable for finite-P₂ probabilities. The coupling-infimum proof gives L(||θ−θ′||+W₂(μ,ν)); for split smoothing L=L₁+1/η. This is weaker in metric than the printed W₁ claim, which is not formalized.

checks.claim: The finite-particle system converges to its mean-field limit at order N^(-1/2).
checks.status: constructed iid uniform L² / one-time W₂ replacement proved
checks.note: The actual mean-field reference and every N-particle physical-coordinate process are constructed from a specified P₂ latent law and deterministic initial parameter. Genuine product initialization and independent canonical Brownian paths supply the exact force variance and noise scale. Compact-horizon force continuity chooses a finite coefficient before ∀N. The theorem retains the actual particle equation and proves uniform timewise L² and finite one-time tagged W₂ error C_T/√N. This uses a different process norm from E sup_t in C.2; neither generally dominates the other. exchangeability alone is insufficient and no pathwise strong-SDE/PDE conclusion is asserted.

checks.claim: The smoothed mean-field dynamics converge to the unsmoothed dynamics with the displayed rate.
checks.note: With globally K-Lipschitz smooth g₂ and gradient constant L₂ (derivable from original U and g₁ smoothness), both actual split/original L² integral solutions are constructed. Uniform score defect ηL₂K and common-input Grönwall give sup_t||Yη−Y||₂≤η*C_T. This is weaker in process norm than the square root of E sup_t||error||² in C.3; pathwise strong-SDE/PDE claims are not made.

checks.claim: The second-order term in the displayed proximal Taylor expansion has the wrong sign.
checks.note: For the scalar quadratic the exact expansion has +λ²x. This diagnoses the local algebra, not a counterexample to the final globally Lipschitz theorem.

checks.claim: An O(λ³) pointwise proximal expansion can be integrated to give the displayed marginal remainder.
checks.status: not justified by the stated data; avoided
checks.note: Twice differentiability almost everywhere and the stated moment bound do not themselves supply a uniform integrable Taylor remainder. The formalized replacement uses a uniform value gap.

checks.claim: The fiberwise regularity and Hessian claims need the intended measure and matrix order.
checks.note: Ambient Lebesgue restricted to a fixed parameter fiber vanishes in positive parameter dimension; latent Lebesgue is the meaningful intended fiber measure. A convex Hessian is positive semidefinite, while I+λH is positive definite. The replacement theorem needs neither condition.

checks.paper_location: Corollaries A.11–A.13, pp. 22–24; Theorem A.15, p. 25
checks.claim: The geometric error floor is finite at λ=γ/(1−mγ).
checks.note: At the displayed upper endpoint q=1 and the denominator is zero. The formalization retains the finite geometric sum or uses strict q<1 for an error floor.

checks.claim: The discretization constant is claimed independent of λ.
checks.note: The formal theorem displays L₁+1/λ explicitly. This is a conservative proved estimate, not a proof that all possible λ-uniform estimates are false.

checks.claim: The listed complexity rates and experiment-specific proximal approximations follow from the stated results.
checks.status: PIPGLA iteration-count correction; experiments not certified
checks.note: For the fastest admissible choice λ=γ, the source transient is (1−mγ)^(n/2)W₀. For 0<mγ<1 and 0<ε<W₀, making this term at most ε requires n≥2log(W₀/ε)/[−log(1−mγ)]. Thus for fixed nonzero W₀ and γ of order ε²/dₓ, the required count from this bound is of order dₓ/(mε²)*log(1/ε), rather than Table 1’s essentially logarithmic count. The table omits the inverse-step factor. This is an elementary consequence of the printed theorem, not a Lean-certified complexity theorem or an algorithmic lower bound. The source’s smoothing-dependent constants also need separate analysis. Experimental numerical approximations and nonconvex/extended-valued models remain outside the theorem coverage.

checks.claim: An averaged pairwise proximal map need not minimize the lifted proximal objective, even for a globally Lipschitz convex penalty.
checks.note: For g₂(θ,x)=|θ−x|, N=2 and λ=1, the two genuine pair-proximal outputs are certified and their averaged output has strictly larger lifted objective than an explicit competitor. The direct particle energy inequality supplies the estimate required by the proof.

checks.paper_location: Corollary A.6, p. 18; separate theorem here
checks.claim: A finite-time PIPULA bound around its smoothed marginal center follows under genuine strong convexity of the original potential.
checks.note: The actual envelope has modulus m/(1+mγ), and its admissible ULA step is derived. No original-center rate is asserted. The conservative explicit bias coefficient grows as γ tends to zero, so this does not establish the published O(√γ) approximation claim.

checks.paper_location: Additional supporting theorem in this repository
checks.claim: The actual PIPGLA recursion contracts two synchronously driven runs.
checks.note: The pairwise proximal map remains nonexpansive after shared-parameter averaging. The sharp forward-step contraction and induction give the factor (1−mγ)^k. This does not supply the paper’s equilibrium bias bound.

checks.claim: The smooth-part Gibbs moment can be controlled uniformly in the smoothing scale.
checks.note: At the actual reference mode the two gradients cancel. Sharp concentration and bounded Moreau gradient imply E||∇F₁||²≤2L²D/m₀+2K₀²; inverse-scale smoothness is not used as the local drift constant.

checks.claim: Future Brownian increments are orthogonal to the actual adapted reference drift.
checks.note: Past/future independence, independent initialization, constructed-solution adaptedness, zero Gaussian mean, and finite L² moments yield the zero mixed term.

checks.claim: The actual Gaussian splitting laws obey a derived squared Wasserstein recurrence.
checks.note: The stationary reference and every stochastic input are constructed for each input coupling. Finite output transport is established before real conversion, and the infimum is taken without assuming an optimal coupling.

checks.claim: Equal-step PIPGLA has an O(√γ) transport error with an explicit γ-independent coefficient.
checks.note: The squared error is at most (1−mγ)^n W₂(initial,ΠNγ)²+(γ/N)C_N, with m₀=Nm,L=NL₁,K₀=NK and δ=NγK²/2. This does not claim the source’s exact numerical forcing.

checks.claim: Changing the positive proximal parameter changes the actual chain by a controlled amount.
checks.note: True minimizer sensitivity gives K|λ−η| at one proximal step and K|λ−η|/(mγ) for the shared-noise chain. For γ≤λ≤γ/(1−mγ), mγ<1, this is at most Kγ/(1−mγ), including the upper endpoint.

checks.claim: A uniformly bounded subgradient selection implies global value Lipschitzness.
checks.note: Supporting planes at both endpoints give |g₂(x)−g₂(y)|≤K||x−y||. Thus the source’s bounded minimal-subgradient premise supplies the K-Lipschitz hypothesis used by the replacement theorem.

checks.claim: The expected-parameter and pointwise-latent mean-field equations admit actual continuous L² integral solutions.
checks.note: The averaging operator, actual gradient drift and its 2L Lipschitz constant are constructed. Picard gives finite-horizon solutions; constant initial parameter and latent-only Brownian input give deterministic parameter evolution and the actual latent-law identity. Pathwise strong-SDE, adaptedness and PDE claims are not asserted.

checks.claim: The empirical mean-field force has centered variance1/N under actual iid sampling.
checks.note: The product probability space, independence, finite moments, centered mean and mixed-inner-product cancellation are all derived. This corrects the use of exchangeability alone as a substitute for controlled initialization; the variance identity alone is not presented as chaos convergence.

checks.paper_location: Appendix A.3, p. 18; A3 and B1
checks.claim: If A3 is applied to the g₁=0 full-potential representation, global Lipschitzness and a positive B1 deficit cannot coexist in positive dimension.
checks.note: The true proximal residual is globally bounded by K, whereas B1 implies positive strong monotonicity μ/γ; arbitrary-distance test points give a contradiction. This does not reject a different reading that retains an independent original split decomposition. The separate PIPULA theorem drops full-potential global Lipschitzness.

checks.claim: The particle initialization and Brownian inputs have the intended actual laws and independence.
checks.note: The specified latent law is paired with a canonical Brownian source, independent of initialization. Finite products give iid copies; injective selection gives independent parameter and latent Brownian paths. The parameter noise norm is derived as √(2dθt/N). No variance or noise estimate is assumed.

checks.claim: Actual tagged particle pair laws converge to the constructed mean-field law at rate N^(-1/2) on each finite horizon.
checks.note: The final theorem retains actual integral equations, the iid initial pair and the canonical particle Brownian input. The same constructed coupling bounds each one-time W₂ by C_T/√N, after proving the distance finite. It does not assert Wasserstein convergence on path space or the source’s different expected supremum norm.

verdict: Corrected MYIPLA, PIPGLA and MYPGD original-center theorems are proved for their actual Gaussian recursions, with changes in constants and smoothing rates displayed. Actual continuous L² mean-field equations, a finite smoothing comparison, and an iid tagged-particle limit in uniform timewise L² and one-time W₂ are constructed. This remains a partial paper formalization: the exact heat-flow formula, stronger Taylor asymptotics, expected path-supremum statements and PDE claims are not reproduced.
